units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 98">Gen. R. s. 98</cite> <he>חיויא דבעי למִיכַּת וכ׳</he> the serpent that is to bite my son.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:49">Y. Peah I, 16ᵃ</cite> bot. [read:] <he>אילולי דאתאמר … נְכוֹת לא הוינא נָכֵית</he> had I not been told from on high, ‘bite’, I should not bite.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 7:1:4">Koh. R. to VII, 1</cite> <he>מאן דנַכְתֵיה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00411"><he>דְּחֵיל</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Gittin 67b:11">Gitt. 67ᵇ</cite> (expl. <cite ref="S00574"><he>קורדייקוס</he></cite>) <he>דנכתיה חמרא וכ׳</he> young wine from the press has bitten him (made him delirious).
B. Mets. 60ᵇ נשך איכא דקא נכית ליה וכ׳ it is neshekh (usury, v. נֶשֶׁךְ), for he bites (injures) him, by taking from him something which he (the creditor) had not given him; a. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 21:6">Targ. O. Num. XXI, 6</cite>, v. supra.—
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 35b:20">Ab. Zar. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>היה מְנַכֵּית ואכיל וכ׳</he> took a bite and ate of the bread (of a non-Jew) &c.
<cite ref="Yevamot 76a:3-7">Yeb. 76ᵃ</cite> <he>מייתינן … ומְנַכְּתִינָן ליה וכ׳</he> we get a big ant and let it bite (insert its head into the opening) and cut its head off.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 21:9">Targ. Y. II ib. 9</cite>.
